speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've had increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if the pain is constant or if it comes and goes, and does it worsen with activity or rest?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoid Osteoma. The severe nocturnal pain unrelieved by NSAIDs (ibuprofen) is highly suggestive of a bone tumor, specifically osteoid osteoma, which typically causes night pain relieved by aspirin or NSAIDs but is currently not responding due to insufficient anti-inflammatory effect. I will need to confirm this with imaging.

REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray Left Knee (AP and Lateral)
